answer.label: Spurgeon’s earlier joke — later wording
answer.sourceLine: Quote Investigator credits Spurgeon with the earliest located family member, an 1878 report saying two committee members were ill in bed. It prints this display’s exact absent-men version from Herbert Beerbohm Tree’s notebook extracts published in 1920. Spurgeon’s priority for the joke family does not verify this exact wording as his.

author.name: Charles Haddon Spurgeon
author.heading: About Charles Haddon Spurgeon
author.bio: Charles Haddon Spurgeon was a British Baptist preacher associated with London’s Metropolitan Tabernacle. His sermons and devotional books reached readers far beyond his congregation. Collections such as The Salt-Cellars also transmitted proverbs, so a phrase appearing in his books need not be his invention.

context.heading: The setting behind the words
lead: The 1878 newspaper report places Spurgeon at a Baptist Union gathering advocating continued progress. His committee joke leaves one person free to take the reins and move the work forward. Later variants change sickness into absence while keeping the joke’s preference for decisive individual action. Quote Investigator comparison ↗
